newsitem.title: FRANCE: French fin min optimistic on growth - deputy.
newsitem.headline: French fin min optimistic on growth - deputy.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn told a French parliamentary committee on Wednesday that he was optimistic on the prospects for French growth, Socialist parliamentary deputy Jean-Pierre Balligand said.
Balligand told reporters Strauss-Kahn had told the parliamentary finance committee that growth could be above three percent by the end of the year.
He had argued that growth would be driven by restocking after huge destocking in 1996, while there were also signs of movement on semi-finished goods.
But Balligand, who left before the meeting finished, said Strauss-Kahn had given no forecast for the public deficit this year.

"He argued above all that the (previous government's) presentation on three percent was false," he said, adding that without the transfer of funds from France Telecom this year the previous government would never have succeeded in reducing the budget to three percent of gross domestic output.
